req.title: Reject wrong method on /delete
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than DELETE on /delete.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /delete must return HTTP 405 for any method other than DELETE. We need: (1) a positive test confirming DELETE returns 200, (2) negative tests confirming GET/POST/PUT/PATCH return exactly 405, and (3) boundary tests covering the edge of the allowed-method set. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (405 not >=400), testing both sides of the method-allowed boundary, and verifying the correct method still works. Each test is self-contained using Flask test_client().

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_method_returns_200():
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'args' in data
    assert 'headers' in data
    assert 'origin' in data

test_delete_method_returns_200()

tests.name: test_delete_boundary_only_allowed_method
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
Send GET (just outside allowed set) -> expect 405
Send HEAD (adjacent method, not in allowed set) -> expect 405 or 200 (Flask allows HEAD for GET routes, but /delete is DELETE-only)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-011: boundary between allowed (DELETE=200) and disallowed (all others=405)
BVA: test the single allowed method and its immediate neighbours in method space
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_boundary_only_allowed_method():
    r_delete = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r_delete.status_code == 200

    r_get = client.get('/delete')
    assert r_get.status_code == 405

    r_post = client.post('/delete')
    assert r_post.status_code == 405

    r_put = client.put('/delete')
    assert r_put.status_code == 405

    r_patch = client.patch('/delete')
    assert r_patch.status_code == 405

test_delete_boundary_only_allowed_method()

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_response_payload_exact_keys():
    r = client.delete('/delete?foo=bar')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert set(['url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json']).issubset(set(data.keys()))
    assert data['args'] == {'foo': 'bar'}

test_delete_response_payload_exact_keys()
